This map shows the Republic of China's territorial claim: the whole mainland, plus Mongolia and slivers of Russia, India and Burma. The claim was real. It is also out of date in a way almost nobody mentions.

a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ Start with the odd part: the 1947 constitution never draws the border. It only says the national territory cannot be altered except by the National Assembly, which left the question of what that territory actually is permanently open.

2/ Mongolia is the headline, and the history is messier than the map. Under the 1945 Sino-Soviet treaty, and after a Mongolian independence referendum, the Nationalist government formally recognised Mongolian independence in January 1946.

3/ Then the civil war ended. In 1952 the ROC accused Moscow of violating that treaty; the following year the Legislative Yuan voted to abrogate it. Mongolia went back onto official ROC maps and stayed there for another half century.

4/ The claim had teeth. The ROC held China's UN Security Council seat until 1971 and used it to keep Mongolia out. Its only veto in its entire UN membership was cast in 1955, against Mongolian admission. Mongolia got in in 1960.

5/ In 1993 the Legislative Yuan asked the courts to just say where the border was. The Judicial Yuan declined: Interpretation 328 ruled the constitutional territory was beyond judicial review. The question was dodged, not answered.

6/ The maps changed in 2002: an Executive Yuan order removed Mongolia from ROC jurisdiction, the interior ministry stopped printing it as ROC land, and that October Taipei recognised it as independent. The commission that ran the claim closed in 2017.

7/ The mainland claim is the one that hasn't moved. Renouncing it is widely read in Beijing as a declaration of independence, so it survives less as ambition than as a line Taipei can't safely erase.
